llm.summary: The single most important fact this morning is that the 10-year Treasury is at 5.33-5.34%, the highest since 2002, with UK 30-year gilts above 6% for the first time since 1998 and the dollar at a 16-month high — a global term-premium/supply shock that is no longer about the Fed path, since it is happening *after* a soft core PCE print. Micron delivered a revenue surge and the stock is not being rewarded, which is the cleanest tell in the tape: in a 5%+ risk-free world, even excellent AI-cycle fundamentals buy you no multiple. The oil story has mutated from a crude supply scare into a refining/distillate crisis — Brent near $100, Chinese refiners reportedly banning October fuel exports, and the White House reportedly asking Germany and France to release diesel stockpiles — which is inflationary in exactly the component that feeds headline CPI and term premium, yet Energy sector rotation cooled from +23 to +10, so capital is not confirming the commodity. Breadth is pathological: Technology +57 and Health Care +13 against Financials -72, Consumer Discretionary -83, Materials -84, Utilities -85 and Real Estate -87, with small-cap flows negative and growth beating value by 75 points. Underneath the AI trade two new cracks opened: Nvidia's financing guarantees to chip buyers are drawing credit-risk scrutiny as neocloud debt builds, and Google simultaneously shipped Gemini 4 Argon and is launching its own TPUs into orbit with SpaceX while DeepSeek and Huawei attack CUDA — the first credible multi-vector challenge to the monopoly premium. Michael Burry's disclosed puts on NVDA, MU and PLTR and Gundlach's 'hollow tree' warning are now part of the narrative, which matters less as a forecast than as evidence that the crowding is recognized. Own chokepoints — HBM bits, barrels and refined product, electrons, payment rails, agent governance — and own nothing that requires the long end to fall.

market_thesis.short_term: Days-to-weeks: the tape is a standoff between accelerating Technology flows and a bond market at 24-year yield highs, and the resolution risk is to the downside because the marginal buyer of equities is now paying 5.3% to do nothing. Micron's unrewarded beat is the template — good AI numbers are necessary but no longer sufficient, so expect violent single-name dispersion rather than index trend. Energy is the awkward position: Brent near $100 on the China fuel-export ban and stalled US-Iran talks, but sector rotation decayed from +23 to +10, meaning the barrel is working and the equity sleeve is not yet being funded; one more day of flow decay turns EOG/COP/OXY into a carry-and-wait rather than a momentum holding. Gold and bitcoin stay broken (BTC below $84k) for as long as nominal and real yields rise on good inflation news. Anything needing lower mortgage rates — housing, REITs (Real Estate -87), small caps — should be left alone; the jobs report is the next catalyst that can either break the hike narrative or confirm a stagflationary distillate-led inflation impulse.
market_thesis.medium_term: Months: the AI capex cycle keeps running into a 5%+ discount rate, so the market will continue to pay only for AI monetizers with cash conversion (memory, networking, security, power, the agent control plane) and defund AI spenders, levered neoclouds, and all rate-sensitive sleeves. The emerging medium-term risk is not AI demand but AI *credit*: Nvidia's vendor financing guarantees, neocloud debt, and real-estate-companies-buying-GPUs (La Rosa) are textbook late-cycle circularity, and the first funding accident in that chain would de-rate the entire complex faster than any demand miss. Competitive dilution is now real — Gemini 4 Argon, Google TPUs in orbit, DeepSeek/Huawei attacking CUDA — which compresses the probability of permanent monopoly economics even if unit volumes keep growing. Macro drifts to a Contraction/Goldilocks barbell (Contraction 28 and rising +6.4, Reflation 22 and falling -6.6): the market has stopped equating high yields with strong nominal growth. Expect consumer bifurcation to widen further, with value retail and the top-quintile wealth-effect spender both working while the median household and anything credit-funded deteriorates.
market_thesis.long_term: Years: a persistent ~5% risk-free rate permanently re-rates owners of physical and digital chokepoints above narrative-priced asset-light stories. Three structural lines are compounding. First, compute and energy have fully merged into one asset class — Korea's reported $200bn into US nuclear, LNG and gas power, Russia militarily targeting Ukraine's grid, drone attacks on a UAE nuclear plant, and Google siting data centers in orbit all say the same thing: generation, fuel, transmission and siting regain pricing power lost for forty years, and energy security is now sovereign capex rather than commodity cyclicality. Second, whoever defines identity, delegation and runtime containment for autonomous agents collects a toll on every enterprise deployment; Nvidia is building that reference architecture in the open while regulation arrives piecemeal and locally (California banning AI 'robo bosses'), so the private standard wins first and labour law follows. Third, market structure is being unbundled across access, venue and time simultaneously — SEC proposals plus an investor exam to open private markets to retail, Schwab listing on the Texas Stock Exchange, GCash's Manila IPO — which durably advantages exchange, broker and rail owners over traditional asset gatherers, and quietly raises systemic risk by moving illiquid assets into retail hands late in a cycle.

short_term: Spending is being funded by paper wealth, not income: robust consumer spending and record racehorse prices sit alongside 12-year-low confidence (81.9) and 9.3 million student-loan defaults — the top two quintiles are monetizing AI gains while the bottom half is in arrears.

Housing demand is being converted into rental and renovation demand: mortgage rates at the highest since 2023 freeze transactions, so households redirect the housing budget into staying put, remodelling, and shorter-duration consumption.

Mobility and freight costs are rising at the diesel pump rather than the crude barrel; a distillate squeeze taxes commuters, truckers and e-commerce delivery more than it taxes gasoline-exposed consumers.

Investors want AI exposure without AI agency: agentic AI can trade but surveys show most investors won't let it handle their money — trust, not capability, is the binding constraint on fintech automation.

Retail is chasing access over diversification — rising searches for stablecoins, cloud ETFs and chip fabs, plus eagerness for newly opened private markets — classic late-cycle appetite for complexity.

Enterprises are buying safety and governance before they buy more capability: Nvidia's agent safety stack, Palo Alto's record valuation and Cybersecurity topping the flow ranking show the budget is shifting from experimentation to containment and audit.
Firms are retrofitting themselves into AI stories — a real estate company buying GPUs and considering selling its real estate operations is the purest signal of narrative-driven capital allocation.
long_term: Energy security and electricity reliability become consumer-visible needs, not utility back-office concerns; households and governments will pay a premium for firm power as grids become military and AI targets.

Knowledge work is being re-contracted around agents with identity and delegated authority — the durable need is provable accountability for machine decisions, which creates permanent demand for identity, logging and containment layers.
Labour's response to AI shifts from wage bargaining to governance rights: California's ban on AI 'robo bosses' marks the start of a decade of rules about who may be managed by software.

Convenience migrates from apps to autonomous delegation, but only where liability is clear — healthcare billing already run by AI (with patients bearing the cost) will force a transparency backlash and a compliance industry.
Status and security expression shifts toward hard, scarce, income-producing assets and private-market access as 5% nominal rates make yield fashionable again after fifteen years of growth worship.
Compute becomes a sovereign utility sited by power and politics — including orbit — changing where people work, where industry locates, and which regions capture the next wave of jobs.
Payments fragment toward programmable money: stablecoin curiosity turning into stablecoin products threatens the pure toll economics of card networks over a decade, not a quarter.
